claim: *Three correspondence patterns.* Derivation extracts models from implementation; generation produces implementation artifacts from models; traceability connects representations maintained independently. Each relationship covers selected properties or artifacts rather than necessarily determining the entire implementation.
topology: Derive points upward from implementation to models. Generate points downward from models to generated implementation artifacts. Trace curves downward to bind related elements; check curves upward to evaluate correspondence where decidable. Thin vertical rules separate peer modes; internal graph examples have undirected structural edges.
bw_encoding: Only the generated/corresponding implementation portion and small table headers use light gray; all model and implementation containers remain white. Other implementation decisions remain visually separate and are not labeled degrees of freedom.
redesign: Author-requested three-column redraw distinguishes authority, correspondence direction, and the limited implementation surface governed by generation or maintained correspondence. The derivation implementation is not artificially divided. Separate curved trace and check arrows distinguish binding related elements from evaluating decidable correspondence. Repeated panel footer prose and internal figure title are omitted.
alt: Three columns distinguish correspondence patterns. Derive: implementation is authoritative and an upward arrow extracts selected models from implementation; the implementation is shown without a represented-portion division. Generate: models are authoritative and a downward arrow produces a generated portion of implementation, leaving other decisions open. Trace and check: neither fully determines the other; one curved arrow traces related elements and the opposing arrow checks correspondence where decidable. A shaded corresponding portion is maintained and checked while other implementation decisions remain separate. Each model box shows the same small graph and state/response table.
